newsitem.title: USA: High waters hamper Illinois River barge traffic.
newsitem.headline: High waters hamper Illinois River barge traffic.

text.p: Rising water fed by heavy rains last Thursday and Friday has snagged barge traffic on the Illinois River and forced the closure of several locks, a U.S. Army Corp of Engineers official said.

"Barge traffic from Starved Rock up through Dresden Island Lock, near Morris, Ill., is on hold right now," said Rick Granados, chief of Lock and Dam section for the Illinois Waterway Project, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.
He noted Marseilles Lock at Marseilles, Ill., and Starved Rock Lock near Utica, Ill., were currently closed to navigation due to high waters.

"The wickets (a series of submerged panels) are down at Peoria Lock and LaGrange Lock near Beardstown (Ill.,)" but barges were able to move," Granados said, adding there was not a lot of traffic out there now.

U.S. cost, insurance and freight (CIF) corn values rose by two to three cents a bushel in the nearby positions on Monday, supported by possible problems loading barges on parts of the Illinois River, export sources said.
"That is what we are seeing now," one exporter said.
As of 0800 CST, the Illinois River at Peoria was at 23.5 feet compared with 20.6 feet on Sunday at 0800 CST. Flood stage is at 18 feet at Peoria, the Corps said.
He said he expected barge traffic to be up and running at Dresden Island, Marseilles and Starved Rock locks within the next few days.
Granados said the waters are going down right now on some parts of the river but the water has not yet crested at Beardstown, Ill., and the river at Peoria is not expected to crest until Thursday.
